skill.description: Design and coordinate multi-agent Claude Flow swarms for research, development, testing, analysis, recovery, monitoring, and reusable automation workflows.

security_audit.summary: Most alerts are false positives caused by Markdown fences, inline names, documentation links, and ordinary guidance. Four findings are confirmed because examples execute community npm packages through global installation or unversioned npx commands. No prompt injection, exfiltration intent, or malicious behavior was found.

remediation.issue: The prerequisite globally installs a prerelease package and registers it as an MCP server.
remediation.suggestion: Pin an audited release by exact version, prefer a project-local installation, and require confirmation before registration or lifecycle script execution.

remediation.issue: CLI fallbacks use npx without an exact package version and can create persistent output.
remediation.suggestion: Add exact versions, describe expected file changes, and require user approval before package download, execution, or filesystem modification.

content.value_statement: Complex projects need coordinated agents, dependencies, memory, and recovery. This skill provides reusable Claude Flow patterns for research, development, testing, analysis, and monitoring.
actual_capabilities: Initialize mesh, hierarchical, star, or ring topologies with agent limits and execution strategies.
Define specialized agent teams for research, full-stack development, testing, and code analysis.
Coordinate parallel, sequential, batch, and dependency-aware tasks through Claude Flow MCP tools.
Persist namespaced memory, snapshots, backups, and workflow state across coordinated sessions.
Monitor swarm health, metrics, costs, bottlenecks, and execution results.
Configure recovery, scaling, load balancing, reusable workflows, and event-driven automation.
limitations: Requires Claude Flow and compatible MCP tools or CLI access.
Examples contain placeholders and undeclared variables that need adaptation before use.
Named agent capabilities do not guarantee that every external integration is configured.
CLI examples may download packages and write files, so review commands and pin versions before execution.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Parallel Research
use_cases.description: Assign source discovery, validation, analysis, and synthesis to specialized agents, then combine results into a structured report.

use_cases.title: Deliver a Full-Stack Feature
use_cases.description: Coordinate architecture, backend, frontend, database, testing, review, documentation, and deployment tasks with explicit dependencies.

use_cases.title: Run Distributed Quality Analysis
use_cases.description: Parallelize unit, integration, performance, and security checks while centralizing monitoring and final reporting.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Research Swarm
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a mesh swarm plan for [research topic]. Define agent roles, parallel tasks, validation steps, dependencies, and the final report structure.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a focused research project

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Feature Development
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a hierarchical swarm for [feature]. Assign architecture, implementation, testing, review, and documentation tasks with clear dependencies and completion criteria.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate software delivery across specialist agents

prompt_templates.title: Build a Testing Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a star-topology testing swarm for [system]. Cover unit, integration, end-to-end, performance, and security testing with monitoring and reporting.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced quality assurance for a defined system

prompt_templates.title: Engineer Resilient Automation
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a reusable swarm workflow for [objective]. Include topology changes, memory namespaces, checkpoints, retries, scaling rules, metrics, failure recovery, and approval boundaries.

output_examples.input: Plan a swarm to research current database options for a regulated application.
output: Topology: mesh with two researchers, one compliance analyst, one performance analyst, and one report writer.
Flow: gather sources in parallel, validate evidence, compare constraints, then synthesize a cited recommendation.
Controls: use approved sources, record uncertainty, and exclude unsupported product claims.

output_examples.input: Coordinate delivery of account recovery for an existing web application.
output: Topology: hierarchical with an architect coordinating backend, frontend, database, testing, security review, and documentation roles.
Dependencies: approve threat model first, implement components in parallel, then complete integration tests and review.
Result: a staged delivery plan with owners, acceptance criteria, checkpoints, and rollback requirements.

output_examples.input: Create a recovery plan for a testing swarm that fails during parallel execution.
output: Pause dependent tasks and capture current state, logs, and completed results.
Assess swarm health, isolate the failed task, and retry it sequentially with a bounded attempt limit.
Restore the latest checkpoint when state is inconsistent, then report the failure cause and recovery outcome.

best_practices: Define deliverables, dependencies, and completion criteria before spawning agents.
Assign distinct roles with bounded permissions, shared state rules, and named owners.
Start with the smallest useful swarm, monitor resource use, and scale only when evidence supports it.
anti_patterns: Do not assign duplicate responsibilities without a clear review or reconciliation process.
Do not enable production deployment or persistent automation without explicit user approval.
Do not place secrets, credentials, or sensitive personal data in shared swarm memory.

faq.question: Is this skill a standalone program?
faq.answer: No. It provides orchestration guidance and examples for Claude Flow MCP tools and CLI commands.

faq.question: What must be installed?
faq.answer: Claude Flow is required for the examples. Review the package, pin an exact version, and prefer a project-local installation.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: How should I choose a topology?
faq.answer: Use mesh for collaboration, hierarchical for managed delivery, star for centralized testing, and ring for staged pipelines.

faq.question: Does the skill execute commands automatically?
faq.answer: The document contains executable CLI examples and MCP operations. Execution depends on the agent environment and should require user approval.

faq.question: Can swarm memory store sensitive data?
faq.answer: It can store supplied values, but secrets and personal data should remain outside shared memory unless approved controls are configured.
